item.title: Sen Jim Justice finds way through Senate polarization to bring WWII hero memorial to DC
item.description: Jim Justice reveals how a last-minute conversation with Martin Heinrich broke a partisan logjam to pass the Hershel Woody Williams monument bill.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Jim Justice, R-W.Va., found a way to get something passed unanimously, despite what he rebukes as "romper-room behavior" of political polarization in the Senate.

In an interview Saturday with Fox News Digital, Justice detailed how he worked around the Senate’s bitter partisan divide to get a monument honoring late World War II Medal of Honor hero Hershel "Woody" Williams onto the National Mall.

"I've never seen anything like this, never in my life seen anything to where it is, it is so preposterous," Justice lamented. "You know, no one could make any sense out of what in the world is going on a lot of times."

"I don't know why we don't talk to one another," he added. "I don't know why we're disrespectful to one other."

DEMOCRATS BLINK AS SCHUMER HELPS GOP CLEAR KEY SHUTDOWN HURDLE

Using good, old-fashioned dialogue, Justice's effort ultimately succeeded in getting his first Senate law passed for his late friend. The Williams National Medal of Honor Monument Location Act directs the National Medal of Honor monument to a prominent location within the Reserve on the National Mall.

The legislation is Justice’s first bill as a senator. It honors Williams, a West Virginia native who received the Medal of Honor for extraordinary heroism during the Battle of Iwo Jima and who was the last surviving World War II Medal of Honor recipient before his death in 2022 at age 98. The monument will honor Williams by name while commemorating Medal of Honor recipients as a whole.

The House approved the measure on Aug. 31 after the Senate passed it unanimously in March. The legislation is now awaiting Trump’s signature.

"We're really hopeful he's going to sign it this coming week," Justice said. "There's been a lot to make all that happen and everything, and I can't be more proud."

Justice, describing the partisan fight in the interview, said the path to unanimous approval was anything but smooth.

EXCLUSIVE: NEW AMERICA 250 MONUMENT LETS FAMILIES FIND MILITARY RELATIVES IN SECONDS: 'I HAD TEARS IN MY EYES'

"I mean, we had it shot down," he said, adding, but "I just wouldn’t turn it loose."

"And the reason I wouldn’t turn loose is because it was just real simple: I mean Woody’s unbelievable, or was unbelievable, that’s for sure. But all these Medal of Honor recipients and everything, the ones we’ve lost and all those that are still living, they are so deserving."

Justice described how the measure initially had become caught up in the same divisiveness that has locked up the Senate on a much broader range of issues.

"All we managed to do is keep a food fight going to where – because it was a Republican thing or Republican Jim Justice introducing – well, I’m telling you, if I’m a Democrat, by God, we’re not gonna let that happen and everything," he lamented. "And then it’s just, it’s the same thing on both sides. Way, way, way too much for a guy that’s got white hair and wants to try to get things done."

EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE

Justice said the breakthrough came just before he was preparing to take the matter to the Senate floor with four Medal of Honor recipients present.

"I was about three feet from going into the Senate chambers," Justice recalled. "And we sat down right there, you know, kind of on the steps and really just started talking."

The senator was Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. The two serve together on the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, and Justice said he had developed a personal relationship with Heinrich over the years, including through Justice’s well-known bulldog, Babydog.

SEN RICK SCOTT: AMERICANS WORK FIVE DAYS A WEEK, WHY CAN’T THE SENATE?

"I said, Martin, I don’t understand. I mean, how in the world can we do this?" Justice said. "And I said, Martin, you know, I’m getting ready to go on the floor, and it’s not going to be good. It’s not gonna be good for you. It’s not going to good for a lot of folks and everything. A lot of people are going to be upset. A lot of people are going to be really sad."

Justice said he appealed directly to Heinrich to find a way forward.

"And I just said, Martin, I don’t know any way to tell it other than just to tell you the truth. And you’re a good guy. And I don’t know why in the world we just can’t talk with one another."

Heinrich responded with a blunt explanation of the broader problem, Justice said.

MEDAL OF HONOR RECIPIENT JAMES CAPERS JR. SAYS RECOGNITION IS BITTERSWEET AFTER LOSING 'SO MUCH'

"And he looked right at me, and he said, you know, people here don’t talk to one another," Justice said. "And I really appreciate you doing that, and I’m not going to object."

Justice said the measure then moved "in three minutes, boom, boom, boom, done."

"It was an amazing moment really, and like I said, Martin's a good guy, and I just think that maybe we could all learn from that just a little bit," he said.

"Now we're going to honor, you know, another great, unbelievable, courageous group of people, and it's way, way, way overdue."

HOUSE REPUBLICANS DID WHAT VOTERS ASKED AND WE HAVE THE RECEIPTS. IT’S UP TO THE SENATE

On other issues in the Senate still in gridlock, Justice urged dialogue like that above and for everyone to "grow up."

"Why in the world would you carry on with just childishness, and in all fairness, that's what it is," Justice said. "You can't make sense of it. There's no point in us trying to do that. This is Romper Room behavior. And if there's anything in the world I could do, I wish to goodness that I could tell everybody, you know let's grow up a lot. Let's absolutely grow up and let's behave."

Justice said he does not expect the Senate’s structural problems to be fixed easily, pointing to the 60-vote threshold associated with overcoming a filibuster and arguing that lawmakers have little incentive to change a system that protects the political status quo.

HEGSETH UPGRADES ABBEY GATE MARINES' VALOR AWARDS AFTER 5-YEAR DELAY: 'THOSE DAYS ARE OVER'

"You’ve got a lot of people there that have never had a job," Justice said. "They’ve been there forever, and they’ve never made a payroll."

He said his former chief of staff Brian Abraham once gave him an even simpler explanation for the paralysis.

"I said, ‘guys, we’re really missing something here because we can really get stuff done here and everything,’" Justice recalled. "And he looked right at me, and he said, ‘you don’t understand, do you?’

"People here don’t wanna get something done. All they want to do is just keep it going. Round and round it goes. Fundraiser, fundraiser, fundraiser. Round and around it goes, get reelected, get re-elected."

DAKOTA MEYER TALKS SERVICE, BLASTS CONTROVERSIAL DESIGN FOR GLOBAL WAR ON TERROR MEMORIAL

Justice said the monument fight was especially important because Williams himself embodied the opposite of that kind of self-interest.

"Woody Williams was all about us," he said. "Woody Williams was never about Woody Williams. And he just was an amazing man. I got to know him really well, and we became really good friends."

Williams’ Medal of Honor citation stems from his actions on Iwo Jima, where, under intense enemy fire, he used a flamethrower to destroy Japanese positions and help clear a path for advancing Marines.

Justice said the symbolism of the monument extends beyond Williams and into future generations.

"Now, I’m going to take them there," Justice said of his future descendants. "I’m going to show them this and tell them, maybe I was only a grain of sand, but I had something to do with this. And I really stood up hard for it and everything. We got it done."

item.content:encoded:

Williams died over the weekend after he collapsed following a match at Enjoy Wrestling in Pennsylvania. He was 48.

Rhodes was a part of The Butcher’s All Elite Wrestling debut. The Butcher, The Blade and Bunny appeared from underneath the ring to attack Rhodes after a match. Rhodes recalled the moment in an interview with OutKick Dropkick.

"When I was away from WWE, I actually — him and Blade (also known as Pepper Parks) and Bunny — we had recruited them to do this really fun debut," he said. "He came up under the ring and they beat me up, and I definitely didn't get to spend near enough time with him as a person. But all the things you're hearing about him in terms of how warm and charismatic and interesting — not a guy that needed the gig, he had another gig, and super cultured and intelligent. item.title: I'm the acting secretary of Labor and I'm here to say thank you to the American worker
item.description: Trump's acting secretary of Labor highlights manufacturing growth, apprenticeships and AI job training in a Labor Day tribute to American workers.
item.content:encoded:
For 250 years, American workers have shown the world time and again that they are the best.

From the transcontinental railroad, the skyscrapers of New York City, the arsenal of democracy that won two world wars, and the tech revolution of the last several decades, every stage of American ingenuity and innovation was made possible because we trusted the hard-working men and women of this country to do what they do best:

Build, create, and innovate, and leave a legacy that their children can be proud of.

LIZ PEEK: THE TRUMP ECONOMY IS DOING BETTER THAN THE MEDIA WANT TO ADMIT

So, this Labor Day, as President Donald Trump’s acting secretary of Labor, I want to say thank you.

Thank you for building the homes that we raise our families in.

Thank you for building factories that showed the world the power of industry.

Thank you for building the highways and railroads that tied our communities together.

And thank you for your hard work and perseverance, even as successive generations of governments took you for granted.

Under President Trump’s leadership, I can assure you those days are over. Today, the American worker is at the center of our nation’s economic agenda and of our industrial revival, because every American should be able to work, raise their children and worship God in the communities that their parents and grandparents built for them.

BESSENT CREDITS TRUMP IMMIGRATION POLICIES WITH HELPING RETURN JOBS TO AMERICANS AS WAGE GAINS RESUME

Last month the economy added 162,000 jobs, and we’ve created more than 1 million private sector jobs since President Trump took office.

Instead of leaving factories to rot and rust, we are revitalizing communities by building new ones and heralding a new era of American industrial might.

After years of decline, American manufacturing has expanded for eight straight months. The jobs that were lost overseas are coming back and renewing the communities that were left behind, the economy is growing, paychecks are getting bigger, and more Americans are working than at any point in our nation’s history.

But more importantly, we’re sowing the seeds of a historic economic boom. President Trump has secured trillions of dollars in new investments from companies and countries alike.

ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM

Manufacturing and construction jobs have grown for three straight months. And we’ve expanded opportunities in the skilled trades through registered apprenticeships, to ensure American workers can find dignified and high-paying careers wherever they choose to live.

Instead of treating the advent of artificial intelligence as an inevitable source of job loss, we are developing training programs for AI integration so that this revolutionary technology becomes a source of job creation, business expansion and wage growth.

JENSEN HUANG SAYS AI WILL RESHAPE WORK LIKE THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION AND THE US 'SHOULD ABSOLUTELY LEAD'

American workers once built the rockets that took us to the moon and made advancements in energy production that our ancestors could only dream of. Today, the American worker is taking the world to Mars, achieving lifesaving advances in medicine and exploring the very limits of human potential. All because some brilliant and hard-working Americans dedicate themselves to a mission and see it to completion.

At universities across the country there is an army of young Americans working in the STEM fields ready to take on the tech jobs of the future. And in towns and cities across America, there are millions of young Americans who are eager to help build things and feel a rush of pride when they see the sticker that says, "Made in America."

TRUMP TAPS ACTING LABOR SECRETARY KEITH SONDERLING FOR PERMANENT ROLE PENDING SENATE CONFIRMATION

The greatest privilege of my job as Acting Secretary of Labor is getting to see up close how Americans from Texas to Ohio, to Florida, New Mexico and beyond, are showing the world that we are a hardworking, devoted, patriotic and innovative people.

So this Labor Day, I hope all American workers take a moment to pause and reflect on the important work you do for our country.

At President Trump’s Department of Labor we are using Labor Day as an opportunity to recommit ourselves to ensuring that the American worker remains our nation’s greatest asset and that we are there for them every single day.

Enjoy your Labor Day, and let’s keep working together for the greatest workforce in the world.

item.title: Longevity doctor reveals what matters most for aging well, beyond pricey biohacks
item.description: Dr. Annu Navani shares four low-cost longevity habits rooted in sleep, stress management, nutrition and resistance training for a longer health span.
item.content:encoded:
As "biohacks" like peptides, cold plunges and high-tech wearables grow in popularity, some advocates promote the idea of dramatically extending human life — but others say it’s better to focus on more healthy years rather than living forever.

Dr. Annu Navani — chief medical officer at Le Reve Wellness in San Jose, California, where she leads advanced regenerative and longevity medicine programs — said the biggest myth is that people will be able to live for a "very, very long period of time."

"I do feel we have extended the human lifespan to some extent," Navani, who is also founder of the World Institute of Regenerative Medicine, told Fox News Digital. "So yes, we are making progress, but I think it would be a false promise if we said people would live beyond 120 or 130 years of life."

ARE PEPTIDES THE FOUNTAIN OF YOUTH? DOCTORS WARN HYPE MAY OUTPACE SCIENCE

Instead, Navani said the goal should be to improve the quality of the years people have.

"Longevity medicine is all about adding life to those years, not so much years to life," she said.

Longevity medicine does not necessarily have to mean costly procedures, supplements or biohacks, according to Navani.

For those who have limited time or money, the doctor recommends "starting from within the daily routines of smart practices."

DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE

Navani shared the following four pillars of health that form the foundation of longevity, all of which "don't cost much money at all."

"I think sleep is really understated in terms of its importance for overall health and longevity," she said.

"Studies have shown that at least seven hours of sleep is [generally recommended] for a human being to be able to perform optimally, and has been linked to a good life and a decent health lifespan."

The CDC's guidance recommends seven or more hours for adults, but individual sleep needs vary.

Navani recommends eating at least three or four hours before bed, avoiding stimulating activities such as laptop use, and practicing calming routines like meditation, gratitude or journaling.

Health agencies recommend managing stress through a combination of physical activity, optimal sleep, relaxation techniques, proper nutrition and social connections.

Navani said she begins her day with 20 minutes of meditation and gratitude, which helps calm her mind and relieve stress.

DEMENTIA RISK COULD BE TIED TO YOUR MINDSET AND OUTLOOK ON LIFE, STUDY SUGGESTS

She also recommends meditating in the evening as a way to unwind before bed.

General dietary guidance recommends building meals around a variety of vegetables, fruits, whole grains, lean proteins, and low-fat or fat-free dairy, while limiting added sugars, saturated fat and sodium.

A balanced eating pattern should also be tailored to a person’s age, health needs and preferences, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s guidance.

The CDC recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity — or 75 minutes of vigorous activity — plus muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days per week.

Navani identified high-intensity resistance training as her pick for the most important habit for people in their 50s and beyond. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Studies have shown how it builds bone health and helps musculoskeletal blood flow," she said. "Muscle strength and muscle resilience are linked to health span and longevity, as they impact cardiovascular and neurovascular health."

Navani also identified VO₂ max — which is the maximum amount of oxygen the body can use during intense exercise — as an important marker of overall health and longevity.

"I think VO₂ max is a really important key biomarker that has been shown in quite a few studies to be linked positively to good health and longer lifespan," she said.

The metric is widely used as a measure of cardiorespiratory fitness, reflecting how efficiently the heart, lungs and muscles work together.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

For some older adults or people with health conditions, lower-intensity or supervised strength training may be more appropriate, experts say.

Navani emphasized that it’s never too late to meaningfully improve health span. 

"I often say if you didn't start in your 20s, the best time to start is today," she said. "I have a lot of patients who come to me when they are 55 and 60 and we start the journey then."

The longevity doctor shared her own simple morning routine that she follows to kick-start each day, which includes breaking the first hour of the day into three 20-minute segments.

The first segment focuses on meditation and gratitude.

"The first 20 minutes is just meditating and waking up and kind of just being grateful and thankful," she shared. "That helps calm me down and relieves stress."

The second 20-minute segment is devoted to movement, which includes stretching, exercising and resistance training.

The final 20 minutes are reserved for reading, she said: "I read something that I really want to capture in my brain, something I want to remember."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Navani advised against immediately reaching for the phone or opening email first thing in the morning, instead recommending using that time to read something intellectually engaging.

item.title: Cody Rhodes comes to a crossroads after losing to Randy Orton at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event
item.description: Randy Orton played opossum to perfection at WrestleMania 42, using a low blow and an RKO to steal a pivotal win over a conflicted Cody Rhodes.
item.content:encoded:
How far was Cody Rhodes willing to go to defeat Randy Orton at Sunday Night’s Main Event? That was the question that the WWE Universe waited to be answered as the two met in a WrestleMania 42 grudge match on Sunday at the State Farm Arena.

The short answer? Not far enough.

Rhodes appeared to be trapped between doing what’s right and allowing himself to turn into the villain. After Charles Robinson was knocked out of the match for a few minutes, Rhodes turned up the heat. He bloodied Orton on the outside of the ring and hit multiple Cross Rhodes finishers on Orton. As "The Viper" was trying to pick himself back up, Rhodes was lining Orton up for a punt.

It was going to be the same punt Orton gave Rhodes after he lost the Undisputed WWE Championship match to him in Las Vegas. Rhodes had it perfectly lined up before Orton put his hands up in defense, seemingly trying to surrender. Rhodes looked confused and didn’t exactly know what to do.

Referee Eddie Arango came out to allow Orton to get himself together. As Rhodes pleaded with him to get out of the way, Orton nailed both Rhodes and Arango with a low blow. Playing opossum worked to perfection.

Orton hit Rhodes with an RKO and was able to pin Rhodes for the win as Robinson crawled back into the ring.

Orton picked up a pivotal win, which may put his feud with Rhodes in the rearview for now. Rhodes will have to gather himself. He may be at a literal crossroads right now.

Rhodes has been at the top of the WWE roster in one way or another for the last few years. The losses are beginning to pile up. Sami Zayn pinned Rhodes for the Undisputed WWE Championship at Night of Champions. He then lost to CM Punk for the title at SummerSlam, thanks to Orton.

Now, it appears Rhodes’ quickest way to get back to the title picture is through the Money in the Bank ladder match. The qualifying matches for the event will start this week.

item.content:encoded:
A story from Eric Byrnes’ MLB playing days shows how far confidence and a little borrowed credibility could go.

According to Byrnes, appearing on his "Deuces Wild" podcast, a former Oakland A’s bat boy used an official team cap and his mother’s Cadillac Escalade to pursue a sexual encounter with one of two women who mistook him for the star outfielder.

As the bat boy sat at a red light, two women pulled up alongside him and mistook him for Byrnes. He decided to play along and eventually used the misunderstanding to pursue a sexual encounter with one of the women.

"The girls are like, ‘Eric Byrnes! Eric Byrnes!’ and he’s like, ‘Yeah, what’s up?’" Byrnes recalled. "He ends up getting his knob polished. I’m not kidding. The whole time, this chick thinks it’s f—ing me."

"He told me, and I’m like, ‘Bro, no! What the f—, you can’t do that,’" Byrnes said. "And sure enough, we made an agreement: nice work, congratulations, don’t ever f—ing do it again."

Byrnes, who famously grabbed a rogue fan on the outfield grass during a 2005 game against the Yankees, let the bat boy walk away with a warning. It was a very different kind of sports catfishing in those days.

item.title: Aaron Glenn's Jets bet on Geno Smith and Frank Reich to escape AFC East basement in 2026
item.description: Aaron Glenn's Jets added Geno Smith, Frank Reich, and Minkah Fitzpatrick, but major roster holes raise questions about how far they can climb.
item.content:encoded:
When a franchise goes through coaching turns, multi-year playoff droughts, and bottom-of-the-barrel divisional finishes, finding basic baseline competency becomes the top priority.

Head coach Aaron Glenn enters his second season at the helm, Frank Reich steps in as the new offensive coordinator, and veteran quarterback Geno Smith makes his homecoming under center; New York is aiming to prove that its rock-bottom transitional phase is officially behind them and that they can be a competitive presence in the AFC East.

JETS SAY GENO SMITH DELIVERS 'EXACTLY WHAT WE WERE LOOKING FOR' IN 2026 DEBUT, SO HERE COMES THE OVERREACTION

The Jets endured an abysmal 2025 campaign under first-year head coach Aaron Glenn, finishing dead last in the AFC East with a 3–14 record. Breece Hall provided a rare bright spot, quietly powering his way to a 1,065-yard rushing season to keep the ground game functional. Unfortunately, the team was non-competitive down the stretch, dropping their final five games by 23 or more points each after mid-season trades cleared out key stars. The offense cycled through three starting quarterbacks without a single one breaking the 10-touchdown mark, while star receiver Garrett Wilson missed 11 games due to injury. On defense, the unit set an unwanted NFL milestone by failing to record a single interception all season.

BREECE HALL BECOMES NFL’S THIRD-HIGHEST PAID RUNNING BACK, SO MAYBE JETS OFFENSE WON’T STINK AGAIN

Recognizing that his inaugural staff and roster lacked execution, Glenn reshuffled his coaching staff—hiring former Colts head coach Frank Reich as offensive coordinator and Brian Duker on defense—while general manager Darren Mougey utilized massive cap room and draft capital. The Jets revamped their quarterback room by bringing back veteran Geno Smith to start alongside draft pick Cade Klubnik. There are still major holes they tried to fill, and I’m not sure they did a great job with it.

INSIDE THE NEW YORK JETS' REVAMPED PERFORMANCE FACILITY AND PLAYER DEVELOPMENT STRATEGY

The Jets let quarterbacks Justin Fields and Tyrod Taylor walk in free agency, while trading away depth pieces and clearing house on secondary coverage. They also traded for Minkah Fitzpatrick to try and address the secondary as much as possible.

I suppose it really doesn’t take much for the team to be considered better than last year. Geno Smith looked awful in Las Vegas, but he still should be a better passer than the run-first combination they had of Fields and Taylor from last year. If Smith can be even somewhat competent, Hall might have even more running room. The Jets offensive line ranks 21st according to PFF, so it isn’t exactly that strong of a unit.

Up front, No. 2 pick David Bailey pairs with Joseph Ossai and Will McDonald IV to revitalize the pass rush, while veteran Demario Davis commands the middle. Similar to the offense, the team just needs to create one interception to be better than last year. That doesn’t mean the roster is great, but it does mean there is a fairly easy room for improvement.

JETS FANS BREATHE SIGH OF RELIEF AFTER PRACTICE SCARE FOR $43M STAR RUNNING BACK

With all that being said, there isn’t much reason to think this team gets to five or six wins. The team has a defensive line ranked at 29th in the league. We know teams with good lines tend to fare better. Couple bad lines with a big question mark at quarterback, and a lack of talent, and the Jets shouldn’t be expected to take a huge step forward. Again, that doesn’t mean they can’t improve. It seems like they are trying to take the right steps, but I’m taking the under for their win total this season.

item.title: Dylan Cease's dominant road record makes Blue Jays run line a strong bet against the Athletics

item.content:encoded:
I hope you all are having a great Labor Day weekend.

After this, the sports calendar really heats up as three of the four major seasons begin within the next 60 days, and so do the Major League Baseball Playoffs. We are back to the grind on the diamond today as we have a fairly full slate of baseball, but I've picked one of the last games of the day for us to bet on as the Blue Jays take on the Athletics.

The Toronto Blue Jays have to be one of the more frustrating teams for the fans and the organizational leadership alike. They looked like hot garbage for a lot of the season, but all of a sudden, the team is playing good baseball and once again looks like a threat to the American League.

They still don't have a playoff position that they can rest comfortably in, but as of right now, the team is at least back in contention. They are getting production from many hitters on the roster, and even Vlad Guerrero Jr. seems to be heating up, as he is hitting .350 in September as of Sunday morning. His power is still down, with just eight home runs, but the weird thing is he has hit them all on the road this year.

It isn't just Guerrero who has better work on the road. The main reason, in my opinion, for this turnaround can be attributed to tonight's starter, Dylan Cease. This has been a great year for Cease, and he is probably going to be one of the finalists for the Cy Young Award. At 10-5 with a 2.25 ERA and a 1.04 WHIP, Cease has turned in one of the best seasons of his career.

I've highlighted this in the past, but his road work has been outstanding. He has an 8-1 record, with a 1.54 ERA when he pitches outside of Toronto. Athletics hitters have a decent history against him, but are still just 11-for-43 with 15 strikeouts collectively.

The Athletics were considered to be a dark horse for the American League West this season.

Unfortunately, it seems like injuries and pitching derailed those hopes early in the season. It really doesn't matter as the ownership seems to be building this team for a few years from now instead of production immediately. At roughly 30 games under .500 for the season, they are one of the worst teams in baseball, but do have some bright-spot players.

He has been worse pitching in Sacramento than on the road. To his credit, he has been strong over the past month and a half. Since the All-Star Break, he has thrown 49.2 innings and allowed only 13 earned runs. He has faced the Blue Jays hitters in the past, and he has allowed eight hits over 25 at-bats.

item.description: Baked empanadas at the Spanish Bakery & Cafe have drawn crowds since 1965, connecting St. Augustine visitors to the city's deep Spanish roots.
item.content:encoded:
At the Spanish Bakery & Café in St. Augustine, Florida, a tray of 16 empanadas doesn't necessarily last long. On a busy day, bakery manager Carol Miller said customers can scoop them up as soon as they're made.

"There are times when we'll sell through three trays within an hour, not even," Miller told Fox News Digital. "So, it really depends. There is a lot of craze for these empanadas, and they do go very fast."

The attention may be fueled by tourists, recommendations and social media, but the bakery's empanadas are hardly a new addition to St. Augustine's food scene. Miller said they date to the bakery's opening in 1965.

CENTURY-OLD ITALIAN ICE RECIPE IS CREATING CHILDHOOD MEMORIES FOR A WHOLE NEW GENERATION

"We actually make everything from hand ourselves – the doughs, the mixes, pressing them, everything," she said.

Making enough to satisfy the crowds takes work.

Producing 10 trays using the bakery's former hand-rolling process could consume an eight-hour shift, Miller said. A newer rolling machine has cut that time to about four hours. With 16 empanadas to a tray, that's 160 at a time.

While plenty of customers happen upon the bakery while exploring St. Augustine, others arrive knowing exactly what they want. Miller said visitors mention everything from news coverage to TikTok and Instagram posts as reasons for stopping by to try the empanadas for themselves.

AMERICANS ARE PAYING PEOPLE TO WAIT IN LINE FOR TIKTOK-FAMOUS FOOD

The bakery also draws on its surroundings. Located in St. Augustine's historic district, it offers visitors a connection to the city's Spanish identity.

"I think because we are mainly Spanish culture in the colonial quarter here, it is nice that we go back to our Spanish roots here specifically," Miller said. "On top of that, we are a healthier version since we are baked instead of the traditional fried."

That distinction is particularly appealing in Florida's warmer months, Miller said, when visitors spending the day walking around town or heading to the beach may be looking for something hearty without choosing another fried option.

For people hesitant to order an empanada, customers sometimes incorrectly assume the filling will be spicy simply because it's Spanish cuisine, Miller said.

The bakery, she said, tries to make its food welcoming to the broad mix of people who visit St. Augustine.

Not everyone, however, visits because of the hype.

Alexis Rapchak, a 12-year-old visiting from Ohio on her first trip to St. Augustine, was trying one of the empanadas for the first time. Asked how she'd heard about the bakery, her answer was simple: "I didn't. I just showed up."

But she described it as "really good."

"I really like the dough and the inside," she said. "It's perfect."

item.title: It’s Labor Day, not Union Day. American workers deserve freedom of choice
item.description: Union bosses exploit Labor Day to push coercive policies like the PRO Act, which would repeal right-to-work laws and force compulsory union dues.
item.content:encoded:
As summer comes to an end, many Americans are looking forward to the first celebration before fall: Labor Day. A day to recognize the American worker, whose hard work and dedication make our standard of living possible.

Yet every year, union bosses exploit this American tradition by stealing the spotlight from workers to argue for more coercive powers from the government. Instead of celebrating the workers they claim to "represent," union officials use this day to bullhorn rhetoric and wield political influence that protects their privileged positions.

Unions today are largely built on power backed by the government. Rather than have to earn the support of individual workers, union officials wield federal law to force workers under one-size-fits-all so-called "representation," no matter how strenuously a worker might object. In the 24 states without right-to-work laws that make union financial support voluntary, union officials then legally threaten dissenting workers to "pay up or be fired."

EXPLOSIVE REPORT UNEARTHS PROMINENT UNION MONEY TRAIL LABELED A 'STUNNING BETRAYAL' OF MAGA MEMBERS

Even ardent supporters of forced unionism sometimes admit that union boss powers are often used to the detriment of many of the workers they purport to "represent."

Take former Clinton-era Secretary of Labor Robert Reich, who has never seen a proposal for expanded union boss power he didn’t support. While a Harvard professor of business and public policy, Reich bemoaned changes in the law that "put greater weight on the voluntary aspects of unionism and de-emphasized the necessity for coercion."

"In order to maintain themselves, unions have got to have some ability to strap their members to the mast," Reich explained to an Associated Press reporter.

Years later, none other than former Vice President Kamala Harris similarly conceded that many workers are harmed by one-size-fits-all union monopoly contracts. As then-California attorney general, Harris filed a brief with the U.S. Supreme Court that acknowledged that "unions do have substantial latitude to advance bargaining positions that … run counter to the economic interests of some employees."

FRUSTRATED BLUE-COLLAR UNION BOSSES RIP SOCIALIST POLITICIANS, WARN OF LABOR EXODUS FROM DEM PARTY

Union members understand that they are frequently the victims of union coercion, which is why a recent poll by Rasmussen Media Group found that 79% of current union members agreed with the statement, "Workers should never be forced to join or pay dues to a union as a condition of employment." Nonetheless, union officials continue to push for legislation that will expand their coercive powers.

For example, consider big labor’s top priority in Congress: the so-called "PRO Act." Under the guise of "reform," this bill would repeal all right-to-work laws in the majority of states, forcing compulsory union dues and monopoly bargaining on millions of people across the country. But this isn’t the only provision in the PRO Act that’s anti-worker.

Another controversial provision is called the "card check" method of organizing a union. This allows union organizers to bypass the secret ballot method, which empowers workers with the final say on whether to unionize. Instead, card check lets union agents confront workers in person as many times as necessary to pressure and intimidate them into signing "authorization cards" that are then counted as "votes" for the union.

Another item in the PRO Act limits workers’ ability to hold "decertification" votes to remove unions opposed by a majority of employees. These "blocks" and "bars" can keep workers trapped in forced dues for months, sometimes years, even if they unanimously oppose union "representation." No one could claim this is actually pro-worker.

The ambitions of union officials today are a far cry from the wisdom and warnings of early union leaders, who sought to build union membership on a strictly voluntary basis.

In a 1924 speech to delegates of the American Federation of Labor (AFL) convention, Samuel Gompers, recognized as the father of the union movement in America, said, "I want to urge devotion to the fundamentals of human liberty – the principles of voluntarism. No lasting gain has ever come from compulsion."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Voluntarism, the voluntary union affiliation and financial support from workers, is essential if union bosses are going to be accountable to the workers they represent. This ideal is clearly at odds with the agenda of union officials today, who constantly seek new ways to undermine the rights of workers for political gain.

So, this Labor Day, remember that truly being "pro-worker" means rejecting the rhetoric from union bosses who claim workers must be denied their freedom of choice. After all, it’s Labor Day, not Union Day.

item.title: America’s massive labor crisis started in the classroom, not the workplace
item.description: America has 7 million unfilled jobs, but the workforce crisis didn't start at work. It started in classrooms that stopped teaching character.
item.content:encoded:
America has nearly 7 million unfilled jobs. Some of those positions remain open because employers can't find workers with the right technical skills. But ask business owners directly and you'll hear something different.

Too many candidates can't show up on time; struggle to take initiative or accept constructive criticism. They can’t solve problems without detailed instructions, nor can they handle an ordinary setback without falling apart.

Politicians and pundits might blame globalization, automation or data centers. They're looking in the wrong buildings.

I WORRY LESS ABOUT SCREENS THAN ABOUT THE CHALLENGES TODAY’S TEENS NEVER FACE

This crisis didn't begin in the workplace. It began in the classroom.

I spent years as a teacher and as a school administrator before I ever ran an education nonprofit. I watched this happen from the inside. Schools gradually abandoned one of their most important responsibilities: to build character.

JONATHAN TURLEY: CHICAGO SCHOOLS REWARD PROTEST WHILE STUDENTS CAN'T READ

Too many schools stopped teaching reading, writing and arithmetic, sure. But they also stopped teaching resilience, responsibility, perseverance and initiative. The idea that a child's feelings matter more than her performance became a paramount concern in schools.

The "child-centered" classroom sounds compassionate. Who wouldn't want children to come first? But there is a real difference between putting a child first and teaching her she is the center of the universe.

HARVARD STUDENTS REVOLT OVER NEW GRADING POLICY THEY CALL ‘RACIST’

Educators like me were increasingly discouraged from giving failing grades, from delivering honest criticism or from enforcing meaningful consequences. Participation trophies replaced accomplishment. Inflated grades replaced excellence. Protecting self-esteem became more important than preparing students for adulthood.

That’s backward. A child doesn’t build confidence by being told she’s wonderful. She builds it by doing something difficult and discovering she can succeed. Take away the difficulty, and all you’ve handed her is an unearned feeling of accomplishment, which is not the same thing at all.

CLASSICAL EDUCATION AND AI COULD RESHAPE HOW AMERICA PREPARES ITS CHILDREN

Eliminating homework, lowering standards and minimizing testing might lower stress and ease disappointment, but pressure, deadlines, competition and failure are not obstacles to growth. They are often a student’s greatest teachers.

Instead, too many classrooms became paint-by-numbers exercises: Follow the rubric. Memorize the answer. Don't take risks. Wait for instructions. Too many schools have become unrealistic experiments where students rarely experience meaningful consequences until they leave the schoolhouse.

GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY

Is it really surprising young employees expect so little from themselves? The adults around them expected so little from them for 13 years. This might help explain the rise of "quiet quitting," of constant workplace grievances and of an instinct to look for a lawyer instead of a lesson after receiving negative feedback.

Beneath all of this lies a grave misunderstanding of human nature.

WILLIAM BENNETT, JON HAGE: AI CAN MIMIC A TEACHER, BUT IT CANNOT SHEPHERD A SOUL

Schools try to protect children from disappointment, unfairness, conflict and adversity — as though those realities could somehow be eliminated from life.

But education should prepare students for reality, not shelter them from it.

Children should learn about responsibility instead of envy. Virtue instead of victimhood. Perseverance instead of excuses. They should learn character is built through discipline, humility and personal responsibility.

Without those lessons, students reach adulthood believing every disappointment must be someone else's fault.

I’M A UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT. TRUMP IS RIGHT TO MAKE COLLEGES DELIVER FOR STUDENTS

Then reality arrives all at once.

Business owners regularly describe interviewing graduates with impressive degrees but who expect executive positions before they've demonstrated executive ability. They expect flexibility before responsibility, promotion before performance and praise before productivity. These expectations come with their school diplomas — and the fancier the school, the higher the expectation.

But no matter the school, most American students have been taught how to regurgitate facts without thinking critically. This is why, when asked to solve a problem independently, too many respond: "Nobody told me I had to think about that." When given constructive criticism, they don’t ask how to improve — they ask to speak with HR.

The only reason America's workforce isn't in even worse shape is because we're still benefiting from the work ethic of previous generations — people who believe work is an obligation before it is an emotional experience.

That inheritance is running out.

Schools have devoted enormous energy to social-emotional learning, to identity-based curricula and to lessons centered on collective grievance.

When was the last time you saw a school-wide program dedicated to teaching morality? Or humility? Or courage? Or personal responsibility? Those virtues built America. And they used to define America’s workforce.

Employers are right to be frustrated, but they're aiming their frustration at the wrong target if they only blame young workers. The problem was manufactured long before these graduates ever filled out a job application.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The battle today between personal responsibility and collective grievance didn't begin in corporate boardrooms, on social media or on factory floors. It began in the classroom.

The good news is the solution begins in the same place. Education got us into this mess. Only education can get us out.

item.title: DR BEN CARSON: The woke machine is lying in wait for a political comeback
item.description: Corporate America's woke machinery hasn't been dismantled — it's merely paused, and the midterm elections may determine whether Woke 2.0 returns.
item.content:encoded:
We all remember how bad it got. Just a few short years ago, it felt like every major institution — from corporate America, to media, to universities, to Hollywood, to our own government — had decided that half the population was the enemy. Speech was policed, businesses were pressured, and ordinary Americans found themselves locked out of basic services for holding the wrong opinions.

A lot of people are now saying that chapter is closed. "Woke 1 was crazy," Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez said recently, laughing. Others have triumphantly declared that "woke" has been defeated. I understand the desire to move on. But those of us who lived through the mayhem shouldn’t be so quick to agree. Here’s what actually happened and why the danger hasn’t disappeared.

The woke ideology that pervaded nearly every aspect of public life did not conquer American institutions by force of argument alone. Rather, it spread so rapidly because corporate America, in particular, became a willing and enthusiastic partner.

GOP FRESHMAN FIREBRAND TARGETS GLOBAL CONSULTING GIANT OVER 'PLAINLY ILLEGAL' DEI PRACTICES

Technology companies censored ordinary citizens for what amounted to thought crimes, major financial institutions stopped doing business with Immigration and Customs Enforcement, de-banked Donald Trump and refused to serve lawful gun manufacturers. "Green" initiatives became official policy, with nearly every major financial institution committing hundreds of billions to pursuing renewable energy and refusing to do business with coal companies and others that were on the "wrong side of history."

Public displays of progressive orthodoxy became the price of admission across large swaths of the private sector. Companies understood that those then in political power were prepared to make life difficult for any entity that refused to fall in line, to say nothing of their own employees who could cause immeasurable headaches if executives strayed from the progressive worldview.

What we continued to call free enterprise was, in practice, something closer to totalitarian social control administered at the corporate level. A concentrated group of technology platforms, financial institutions and cultural gatekeepers enforced a political narrative against large portions of their own user base. And rather than face a market cost for alienating half their user base, the sheer scale of these companies, and the regulatory barriers that protected them from true competition, made the costs of ideological experiments nearly invisible to those imposing them. When a handful of firms control the infrastructure of speech, payment, and distribution, market power and narrative power become one and the same. Dissent does not have to be answered — it can simply be excluded.

DAN GAINOR: WE GOT TWITTER/X AS A PLATFORM 20 YEARS AGO AND GLOBAL CENSORS STILL HATE AND FEAR IT

The only reason this apparatus was interrupted is that the American people changed the occupants of power.

President Trump’s 2024 victory put the technology companies on notice. Several of their leaders appeared at the inauguration, some even helping underwrite the event. One major platform executive later publicly conceded that his company had made serious mistakes. But we should not be lulled into thinking these companies have learned their lesson. What we are seeing isn’t repentance, but merely temporary accommodation. The true believers remain inside these institutions: corporate boards, human-resources departments and mid-level management structures are still populated by people deeply committed to racial quotas, oppression hierarchies, green fantasies and the denial of basic biological reality. Should political power shift again, the incentive to reimpose a more aggressive and better-organized version of the same project — Woke 2.0 — will be overwhelming.

THE WOKE LEFT CAPTURED THE SMITHSONIAN. AMERICA NEEDS A PATRIOT TO TAKE IT BACK

This is the deeper danger. When the guts of capitalism can be ideologically weaponized, the ordinary corrective mechanisms of competition stop working. Incumbents no longer have to persuade customers or improve their products; they can simply close the gates. A free market depends on the ability of new entrants to challenge established players on the merits. A free society depends on the open contest of ideas. Both are undermined when concentrated private power decides which competitors and which viewpoints are allowed to exist.

DUKE LAW'S ALLEGED RACE-BASED ADMISSIONS ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT RULING: DOJ

What ultimately checked this power was not the market itself, but the marketplace of the ballot box. The policies that followed the change in administration — ending race-based preferences in federal contracting and employment, restoring the principle of equal protection under the law and ending the use of federal funds for irreversible medical procedures on minors — restored a measure of sanity and forced corporate America to adjust its public posture accordingly. Without that governing sanity, there is little to prevent the return of the previous regime on an even larger scale.

That is why the coming midterm elections matter so greatly, and voter identification is essential. Secure elections are the last reliable check ordinary citizens possess against concentrated power, whether public or private. Political leadership is not a luxury in a free society – it’s the thin line between a country in which the people still rule and one in which a handful of unaccountable institutions decide who may speak, who may bank and who may participate in public life.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

We have been given a reprieve in the current moment. The American people demonstrated that they still possess the power to correct course when they choose to use it. But, as the saying goes, eternal vigilance is the price of liberty. Institutions that spent years enforcing ideological orthodoxy have not suddenly discovered the virtues of pluralism. They have simply calculated that the political climate has temporarily changed. The moment that calculation reverses, the pressure will return – more sophisticated, more coordinated and more confident that it can succeed where it previously overreached.

The founding generation understood that freedom of thought and freedom of expression are not ornamental. They are the fundamental operating system of self-government. When those freedoms are systematically constrained by private institutions that face no meaningful competition and no democratic accountability, the fabric of society itself begins to fray. We cannot afford to treat the recent interruption of this process as a permanent victory when it is really just a pause. What we do with that pause will determine whether the next generation inherits a free country or a managed one.

item.title: Former USCIS official, accomplice charged in alleged $960K citizenship bribery scheme
item.description: A former USCIS official and his accomplice allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 in bribes to fast-track citizenship applications, skipping key checks.
item.content:encoded:
A former senior U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services official and his accomplice are facing charges for an alleged bribery scheme in which they accepted nearly $960,000 in exchange for favors in the processing of immigration benefit applications, including citizenship cases.

The former official, Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu, and his financial accomplice, Adeniyi Akeem Somoye, were arrested on federal charges for their roles in an alleged multi‑year scheme to receive illegal gratuities in exchange for manipulating and expediting immigration applications, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas.

The pair were charged with conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official, and they were arrested on Wednesday.

Investigators found extensive WhatsApp messages between Ganiyu, Somoye and numerous applicants whose immigration cases they handled, including thousands of messages and hundreds of calls.

FEDS BUST ONE OF LARGEST ALLEGED MARRIAGE FRAUD SCHEMES IN US HISTORY INVOLVING 1,000-PLUS CHINESE SHAM UNIONS

Between December 2019 and March 2026, the duo allegedly bypassed standard procedures by pushing applicants who paid bribes directly to Ganiyu, skipping key steps in the immigration process such as criminal background checks, interviews, standard USCIS processing protocols and other reviews, according to prosecutors.

Prosecutors allege Ganiyu altered the USCIS system to fast-track applications in exchange for money.

He allegedly fast-tracked citizenship for Somoye before he approved residency applications for Somoye’s wife and child.

Ganiyu allegedly rerouted applications from USCIS field offices in Minneapolis, Charlotte and Houston, bypassing local supervisors so he could approve them himself.

FEDS SEIZE $40M IN GOLD BARS, CASH, ROLEXES FROM FORMER CIA OFFICIAL WHO FAKED BEING A NAVY PILOT

Ganiyu received about $671,438 from citizenship applicants through Zelle and Cash App, along with $287,830 in cash deposits that prosecutors say were meant to conceal the money’s source, according to court documents, the New York Post reported.

Acting as the alleged financial intermediary, Somoye processed roughly $1.7 million in transfers involving applicants, including through bank accounts, Zelle and Cash App, allegedly keeping a portion of the payments. He also deposited $449,010 in cash, court documents show, according to the New York Post.

The complaint alleges that Ganiyu and Somoye often exchanged money "back and forth" with applicants.

Most of the citizenship applications they handled involved applicants from African countries, according to prosecutors.

According to prosecutors, Ganiyu resigned from USCIS in March, citing "personal reasons," several months before his arrest.

"Selling immigration benefits for cash is a blatant abuse of public trust," U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould said in a statement. "When a federal official puts a price tag on lawful status, we will intervene immediately."

Each defendant faces up to five years in federal prison and a fine of up to $250,000.

item.title: US restricts government travel to Mexican border city over threat concerns
item.description: The U.S. Consulate in Nogales announced restricted government travel to essential daylight movement only over an unspecified threat in Sonora, Mexico.
item.content:encoded:
Travel restrictions have been placed on U.S. government employees in the Mexican border city of Nogales, Sonora, according to officials.

The U.S. Embassy and Consulates in Mexico on Saturday issued a warning restricting government activity over an unspecified threat in Nogales, Sonora, in Mexico.

"Due to threat information, U.S. government activities in, and travel to, Nogales have been restricted to essential movement during daylight hours only," the U.S. Consulate General in Nogales said in a statement.

STATE DEPARTMENT URGES AMERICANS TO AVOID MEXICAN CITY JUST ACROSS TEXAS BORDER

"We are alerting U.S. citizens of this threat and change in posture," the statement continued.

Sonora's State Security Board said it contacted U.S. consular officials after the alert was issued but did not provide information identifying a specific threat. State authorities said they had no information establishing a concrete risk to the public, though they would continue preventive security operations in Nogales.

The alert also reminded Americans that the U.S. Travel Advisory designates Sonora as a Level 3 "Reconsider Travel" area.

Anyone in the area is urged to exercise increased caution and be aware of their surroundings, seek shelter in the event of an incident, notify friends and family of their safety in the event of an incident, follow instructions from Mexican law enforcement, and monitor local media for updates.

U.S. lawmakers also encouraged people in the area to pay attention to the warnings issued by the U.S. government.

"For Americans in or near Nogales - or who may have family members or friends there: please heed the guidance and warnings from the U.S. government," Rep. Andy Biggs, R-Ariz., said on X.

"We are praying for the safety of U.S. citizens and personnel who may be in harm's way," he added.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

It remains unclear what threat in Nogales triggered the security warning.

item.title: Barbara Eden, 95, says she’s ‘okay’ after last-minute cancelation of festival appearance
item.description: Barbara Eden reassured fans after a "sudden illness" forced her to miss the Cinecon Classic Film Festival, revealing a new medication's side effects.
item.content:encoded:
Barbara Eden sparked concern among fans after abruptly dropping out of a Los Angeles film festival due to what was described as a "sudden illness," but the 95-year-old actress later shared a reassuring update on social media.

The "I Dream of Jeannie" star was set to be honored during the Cinecon Classic Film Festival at the Landmark Nuart Theatre on Saturday but pulled out shortly before the event was scheduled to begin.

"We’re sorry to share that, due to a sudden illness, Barbara Eden will no longer be able to appear in person at Cinecon tonight," festival organizers announced in a Facebook post on Saturday.

ROD STEWART CALLED 'TONE-DEAF' FOR ATTENDING WORLD CUP GAME A DAY CANCELING CONCERT DUE TO HEALTH ISSUES

"Barbara is deeply regretful that she had to cancel at the last minute, as she had been very much looking forward to seeing everyone and celebrating with us," they continued.

"We know how many of you were excited to welcome Barbara. We appreciate your understanding and join you in sending her our best wishes for a speedy recovery," they added.

'YOU'RE SO VAIN' SINGER CARLY SIMON SAYS PARKINSON'S AND CANCER DIAGNOSES KEPT HER FROM PUBLIC EYE

Eden later took to Instagram to clarify the circumstances around her absence and update fans on her condition.

"It’s okay everyone! I’m okay!" she wrote alongside a photo in which she was seen standing in front of a painting and smiling. "Oh, my goodness there has been a bit of miscommunication," Eden continued. "I’m not suffering from an illness; my doctor very recently prescribed a brand-new medication that turned out to have some nasty side effects. Due to the discomfort, my doctor ordered me to remain at home until it can be sorted out."

MAYIM BIALIK DETAILS 'NIGHTMARE' AFTER ONE INJECTION OF GLP-1 DRUG LED TO WEEKS OF DEBILITATING SIDE EFFECTS

"What awful timing for this to happen! My deepest appreciation to everyone for the concern," she added. "This is just a speedbump! I expect to be out and about as soon as I’m given the go-ahead!" 

"Again, my love and thanks to everyone for all the concern," she concluded.

Cinecon is a classic film festival in Los Angeles that celebrates vintage movies, rare screenings and stars from Hollywood’s Golden Age. This year’s Cinecon marked the festival’s 62nd edition.

CURATORS AT LIBRARY OF CONGRESS DISCOVER LOST FILM BY LEGENDARY CINEMA PIONEER AFTER SPOTTING 'SUBTLE CLUE'

Eden was scheduled to receive the Cinecon Legacy Award alongside a screening of her 1961 film "All Hands on Deck." She had been expected to introduce the movie with her co-star Pat Boone, who later accepted the Cinecon Legacy Award on her behalf.

The Cinecon Legacy Award is an honor given by the Cinecon Classic Film Festival to entertainment professionals for their lifetime achievements and contributions to the motion picture and entertainment industries.

RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

Eden is best known for starring as Jeannie opposite Larry Hagman in the classic NBC sitcom "I Dream of Jeannie," which ran from 1965 to 1970 and made her one of television’s most recognizable stars. The actress's career has spanned more than seven decades across film, TV and theater.

Her film credits include "Flaming Star" opposite Elvis Presley, "Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea" and "Harper Valley P.T.A." She has also starred in the hit TV shows "Dallas" and "Sabrina the Teenage Witch."

Eden earned two Golden Globe nominations for her performance in "I Dream of Jeannie" and was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1988. She was honored with the Legend Award for Lifetime Achievement at the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards in 2023.

Her last film role was in 2019's "My Adventures with Santa," in which she played Mrs. Claus. The movie's cast also included Denise Richards, Patrick Muldoon and Jamie Luner.

In November 2025, Eden starred in a one-night-only stage production of "Love Letters" at the historic El Portal Theatre in North Hollywood, California.

During an interview with Entertainment Weekly last month, Eden shared that she is still open to acting and hinted that she would be interested in playing a villain.

"I could be really mean," she told the outlet.

item.title: Time is now, Clemson Tigers and Dabo Swinney need to call it quits after historic run
item.description: Dabo Swinney's Clemson Tigers suffered a humiliating 51-10 loss to LSU, raising fresh questions about whether the program needs a coaching change.
item.content:encoded:
It happened again.

It's no secret that I was fairly high on the Clemson Tigers this offseason, at least relative to the nonexistent expectations many pundits had for them this year.

I wasn't picking them to make a deep College Football Playoff run or win a national title, but I figured they would compete for an ACC Championship and be a darkhorse Playoff pick.

THREE TEAMS RANKED OUTSIDE THE TOP-12 OF THE COACHES POLL WHO WILL MAKE THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF

Then the LSU game happened.

It seemed like the pieces were in place for them to at least surprise some folks, but alas, that doesn't appear to be the case.

I blame myself for getting sucked back into the Clemson hype machine, but this article isn't about me.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES ON HOT SEAT: BILL BELICHICK, MIKE NORVELL AND OTHERS FACING MAKE-OR-BREAK 2026

This article is about how it might be time for the Tigers and their all-time winningest head coach, Dabo Swinney, to amicably and gracefully part ways.

Saturday night's 51-10 debacle in Death Valley isn't a reason for panic in a vacuum.

LSU and Lane Kiffin will probably do that to a lot of teams far better than Clemson this year.

But the fact that, once again, the Tigers and Swinney are starting their season off on the wrong foot is a cause for concern.

It seems like ever since Trevor Lawrence moved on to the NFL, Clemson can't seem to sustain any momentum to start the season.

And some of you Dabo defenders may point at the fact that they had to play teams like Georgia and LSU in recent years as a way to hand wave these brutal starts.

HAS NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP PICTURE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL ALREADY CHANGED AFTER A STUNNING FIRST WEEK?

While that does explain some of it, Clemson should still be measured as peers of these programs, so the fact that they are getting embarrassed in these contests is a sign things are slipping out of Swinney's hands.

Of course, these game one losses aren't just happening against title contenders either, as the Tigers famously waltzed into Wallace Wade Stadium to take on an unranked Duke squad in 2023, only to get pounded into submission in a 28-7 loss.

Clemson was a top-ten team that year heading into the season, and though they ended their campaign with nine wins and a Gator Bowl berth, that hardly sounds like something fans of the dynastic program would have signed up for just a few years earlier.

Dabo still has enough talent on his roster to compete in the ACC, and this loss to LSU, while humiliating, does nothing to dash their conference title aspirations, but it is indicative that it's starting to trend in the wrong direction in the western end of South Carolina.

RANKING THE TEN BEST COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHES IN THE COUNTRY AHEAD OF THE 2026 SEASON

His resistance toward the transfer portal would be more forgivable if Swinney was still landing top-five recruiting classes, but that isn't the reality anymore.

The last time Clemson signed even a top-ten class was in 2022, and there have been a few ranked outside the top-20 in that time frame.

That won't get this program where they want to be come January, but I guess that's the better question to ask here.

Where do the Tigers want to be in the grand scheme of college football?

Do they still view themselves as one of the premier powers in the sport? Or are they content with winning eight or nine games a year and occasionally threatening to make the CFP?

Because if they want to be the latter, they may need to start having some tough conversations about the man in the team-issued polo tucked into his khakis.

I'm not breaking any news here, but it might be time for a change at Clemson.

We can all recognize the greatness of Dabo Swinney - as I have done before - while simultaneously admitting that the game may have passed him by.

His recruiting classes are starting to falter. His transfer portal hauls are virtually nonexistent. And several other power players in college football have lapped the Tigers in just a few short years.

I won't speculate what will happen to Dabo or the Tigers the rest of this season.

For all I know, they could rattle off 11 straight victories and make me look like a fool.

It's not likely, but it is possible.

With that being said, all signs point to Swinney and Clemson trending down, and I wouldn't be surprised if this was the last dance between legendary coach and program.

That might have sounded like blasphemy just half a decade ago, but college football is always evolving, and Swinney is a man stuck in time.

And he's hurting the very program he helped take to the mountaintop.

item.title: Bronson Reed returns to the ring leaner and meaner and looking like the future of WWE

The future of the WWE was on full display.

item.title: Michael Rapaport slams 'clown' Macklemore for anti-Israel performance
item.description: Michael Rapaport called Macklemore a "clown" after the rapper chanted "Free Palestine" and performed "Hind's Hall" at Ed Sheeran's MetLife shows.
item.content:encoded:
Michael Rapaport slammed Macklemore as a "clown" after the rapper brought his pro-Palestinian message to Ed Sheeran’s concert stage.

Macklemore, 43, repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall" while opening for Sheeran, 35, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, during shows on Friday and Saturday nights.

On Saturday, Rapaport, 56, who is Jewish and has become one of Hollywood’s most outspoken pro-Israel voices since Hamas' Oct. 7 attack, ripped Macklemore, born Benjamin Haggerty, in a blistering post on X.

BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT'

"Imagine going to see Ed Sheeran & this absolute no talent none singer non rapping non dancing clown Macklemore is opening & because he actually has no act or specific skill set he’s jumping around like dkc carrying on about a genocide that never happened in Gaza," Rapaport wrote, adding "This is a nightmare."

In another critical post on X, the comedian questioned Sheeran’s decision to bring Macklemore on as an opening act.

ED SHEERAN CONCERT WORKERS HOSPITALIZED AFTER FORKLIFT INCIDENT IN DETROIT: REPORT

"So Ed Sheeran is ok with this p--- stain opening up for him? Sweet Ed Sheeran?" Rapaport wrote.

Rapaport also reposted an article about the backlash to Macklemore's political messaging following the concerts, writing, "Calling this dude a ‘Rapper' is disrespectful to any actual ‘Rapper.’"

ISRAEL, JEWS TARGETED WORLDWIDE AS WELL-FUNDED LEFTIST, ISLAMIST GROUPS JOIN FOR ‘NAKBA 78’ PROTESTS

Fox News Digital has reached out to Macklemore and Sheeran's representatives for comment. 

In a video that Rapaport posted from the Friday night show, Macklemore, who wore a keffiyeh tied around his neck, was seen repeatedly chanting "Say free, free Palestine!" while music played as he walked around the stage and held up his microphone.

Macklemore, who will be opening for Sheeran during the U.S. leg of the "Shape of You" singer's "Loop Tour," also delivered a speech in which he said that he wanted to use stages across America to advocate for Palestine.

ISRAELI PM NETANYAHU ARGUES PUBLIC OPINION SHIFT ON ISRAEL 'CORRELATES ALMOST 100%' TO SOCIAL MEDIA

"A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine," Macklemore said in a video shared on social media.

"I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them," he continued.

"I have an 11-year-old daughter, her name is Sloan, she’s here tonight. And if any of you guys are parents, then you know that that love that you have for your kids cannot be put into words, right? I want to see her grow up, I want to see her go to school, to fall in love, to figure out meaning, purpose, joy, her existence on this planet. I want it to be the most beautiful possible." 

"And I think that every single human being that walks this earth deserves that exact same feeling. To know safety and peace before they know the sound of violence, to know the sound of laughter on a playground before planes and bombs, for parents to be able to say bye to their kids in the morning and not have to wonder if this is going to be the last time they kiss their child goodbye."

"And if I let that fear I felt on the plane yesterday stop me from speaking my heart in order to keep my own comfort and the audience’s comfort, that is the day I no longer continue to be on stage," Macklemore added. "So, I say, ‘Free Palestine!’"

RAGE AGAINST THE MACHINE'S TOM MORELLO FACES BACKLASH AFTER SINGING AT NYC ICE PROTEST RALLY

Macklemore concluded his speech by calling for the freedom of other countries, including America, and blasting U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

"I say, free America, free Cuba to the Congo to Sudan to Iran, and all the people in America who have to live in fear because of this terrorist organization, ICE," he said.

HAMAS, HEZBOLLAH FLAGS FLY AT ANTI-ISRAEL PROTEST MINUTES AFTER MAMDANI CONDEMNS TERROR PLOT AGAINST JEWS

Following his speech, Macklemore performed "Hind's Hall," a song inspired by the 2024 pro-Palestinian campus demonstrations," as footage from Gaza, pro-Palestinian protests, images of Israeli soldiers and pro-Palestinian messages were displayed on the stadium’s large screens.

The title of the song refers to Hamilton Hall, the Columbia University building that pro-Palestinian students occupied in April 2024 and renamed in honor of a 6-year-old Palestinian girl killed in the Israel-Gaza war. The lyrics in "Hind's Hall" praised the anti-Israel encampments and protests on college campuses across the country and called out President Biden, the police and the music industry.

RAPPER FACES $2.8M LAWSUIT AFTER AXING OPENING ACT FROM TOUR FOLLOWING HER POLITICAL RANT

Macklemore also repeated his pro-Palestinian messaging during Sheeran’s second MetLife Stadium show Saturday night, again calling for "Free Palestine" and performing his protest song "Hind’s Hall."

While some audience members cheered Macklemore's comments and joined the "Free Palestine" chant, the rapper's performance was met with backlash from other attendees.

One concertgoer said on X that he brought his wife and two daughters to Friday’s show as longtime Sheeran fans, but left disappointed after Macklemore’s set turned political. The fan said his daughters looked "completely confused" when Macklemore began chanting "Free Palestine," adding that he had taken them to "an Ed Sheeran concert, not to have an opening act lecture them about Middle East politics."

He said his family left their seats during Macklemore’s performance and returned after the rapper finished, praising Sheeran’s show as "phenomenal" but criticizing the singer for allowing Macklemore to perform again Saturday. "Friday might have been Macklemore’s decision. Saturday was yours," the concertgoer wrote, adding, "Tonight, you lost four of them. And I suspect plenty more."

Another concertgoer said he attended Saturday’s show in a company suite with 35 other people and was "embarrassed" and "shocked" by Macklemore’s set. The attendee said he had "always been a Macklemore fan," but after the rapper’s "political stunt," he could no longer support him or his music.

"When you go WOKE, you have to be prepared to lose fans," he wrote.

The concertgoer also denounced Sheeran for allowing Macklemore to return to the stage Saturday after the backlash from the previous night.

"After it happened on Friday, it should have immediately been stopped," he wrote, adding that he went to the show to hear "amazing music," not "Free Palestine" rants.

Two other concertgoers told Ynet, the English edition of Israel's largest new website, that they were unfamiliar with Macklemore before the show and unaware that he would be performing.

"We only found out there and we were in shock. It was really horrifying," they said.

"We immediately thought about everything our people have been through and how, even when we’re abroad, we still have to feel this antisemitism," they continued. "It was even harder because friends of ours were killed in the war and murdered at Nova. It was like a knife in the heart to hear him sing that way and hear people cheering."

The concertgoers said that some of the members in their group began crying and left the show before Sheeran's performance.

However, some social media users praised Macklemore for speaking up and expressed their support for the rapper's message.

"Huge respect for Ed Sheeran, but seeing Macklemore use his voice for Palestine made this moment mean so much more," one fan wrote on Instagram. "Respect to every artist who refuses to stay silent and uses their platform to speak up for humanity. Macklemore, we hear you."

"LOVE Macklemore, and good on him using his platform to speak out….his messaging is always spot on. Peace," another agreed.

"Free free Palestine. Love to Macklemore. Stay true," one fan chimed in.

"this was from last night!! I hope you get to perform this again tonight too!" a fan wrote alongside a clip from Macklemore's set.

"So happy we get to witness such history!" one fan commented.

"Honestly I loved this part of the concert !" another wrote.

"Music has always been a vital platform for human rights advocacy, not just mindless escape," wrote one X user. "Calling for peace, safety, and equality for Palestinians, Congolese, and Sudanese isn't antisemitic—it's pro-humanity. Macklemore explicitly stands for collective liberation and love."

"Art has always been political, why are you annoyed at an artist giving context to a song he released about the current state of the world you live in?" another fan commented on X. "Also, he was an opener, they could’ve just skipped his set! Although I hope Macklemore sings it louder next time!"

Meanwhile, the Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling for Macklemore to be removed from Sheeran’s remaining tour dates.

"This was an Ed Sheeran concert – not a political rally, not a protest, and not an activist event," the petition read. "The issue is not whether Macklemore has the right to hold political views. The question is where the line should be drawn when an opening act uses a global concert platform to advance a one-sided political agenda."

Macklemore has been outspoken in his support for Palestinians since the start of the Israel-Hamas war. In November 2023, Macklemore spoke at a pro-Palestinian rally in Washington, D.C., where he said, "I don’t know enough. But I know enough that this is a genocide."

The rapper's political messaging has also sparked backlash before. In 2024, he addressed criticism after saying "f--- America" during a pro-Palestinian charity concert in Seattle, later writing that he remained "unwavering in my support for a Free Palestine."

Israel has been accused by some human rights groups, legal scholars and foreign governments of committing genocide during the war in Gaza due to the scale of Palestinian deaths, widespread destruction and mass displacement.

South Africa brought a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice, which ordered Israel in 2024 to take steps to prevent acts of genocide while the case proceeds. Israel has strongly denied accusations of genocide, saying its military campaign is directed at Hamas, not Palestinian civilians, and that it warns civilians to evacuate ahead of attacks while taking steps to comply with international law.

item.title: Trick Williams wins US title after Lil Yachty survives Baron Corbin at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event
item.description: Lil Yachty survived five minutes with Baron Corbin to earn Trick Williams his rematch, then played a pivotal role in the chaotic title fight.

Trick Williams needed a lot of things to go right at Sunday Night’s Main Event to capture the United States Championship for the second time.

Williams got the match for the United States Championship moments after the match. With the State Farm Arena in Atlanta in full support of Williams, he came down to the ring in style. Corbin was waiting for him and the bell started.
